rationale: Evidence: iteration 7 (kd 0.6, span x = ±0.04, sensor_size 0.012, base_speed 1.5, kp 4.0, ki 0.2, last_direction) is the best raced design at 282.45. Oval finishes rose to 12 of 20 and mean oval progress reached 0.89. Oval steering_oscillation was 0.314, still under the 0.32 revert threshold. Line losses remain about 1.0 on the s-bend and 1.25 on the slalom, so the remaining loss is most likely sensing. Iteration 5 showed that the ±0.06 span cut losses (s-bend 1.00 to 0.25) but cost oval finishes (8 to 7), and the span test at ±0.05 was the planned next step. Iteration 6 rejected sensor_size 0.016 (157.9), and iteration 2 rejected base_speed 1.3, so both stay fixed. Change: keep kd 0.6 and every other value from iteration 7, and move the sensor span to x = -0.05, -0.025, 0.0, 0.025, 0.05 (weights unchanged at -2, -1, 0, 1, 2). Expected result: line losses on the s-bend and slalom fall below 1.0 while oval finishes stay at 10 or more of 20, giving a score near or above 282. Risks: the wider span may reduce oval finishes, as ±0.06 did, and oval steering_oscillation sits close to 0.32. If the score falls below 282, or oscillation exceeds about 0.32, revert to the iteration 7 span (±0.04) at kd 0.6. Do not raise kd above 0.6 in this race. Hypotheses: (a) an intermediate span keeps most of the loss reduction from ±0.06 while retaining the oval finishes lost at ±0.06; (b) kd 0.6 is near its useful limit, so further kd gains are small. Measurements wanted: per-track line_loss_events, max_error and steering_oscillation, plus oval completion and completion_time, so the span effect can be separated from kd.
